out.other_title: Judge accuracy: human debate 84%, human consultancy 74%, AI debate 78%, AI consultancy 80%
out.rationale: Both records discuss debate judge accuracy. The authors say their observations, that the Guard's performance scales with general intelligence rating while Houdini performance stays constant, are consistent with prior work including Michael et al., which they describe as finding that judge accuracy may improve with using better models. Michael et al.'s cited figures give judge accuracy per condition (84% for human debate, 74% for human consultancy, and 78% and 80% for AI debate and consultancy), so they vary the condition rather than the judge's capability. The consistency is the citing authors' reading rather than a shared measurement, so the passages do not show that either record bears on the other's claim; the link is navigation only.
out.scope: proposed SHARES_TOPIC: Debate judge accuracy, which Engels et al. relate to general intelligence rating and describe prior work as finding may improve with using better models, while Michael et al.'s cited result compares judge accuracy across human and AI debate and consultancy; Engels et al. report the Guard scaling on TruthfulQA, with similar scaling on QuALITY and PrOntoQA and mostly flat performance for both Guards and Houdinis on BoolQ, and the cited Michael et al. passage does not state its task

text: The authors report that on TruthfulQA the Guard's (judge's) performance in their LLM debate game scales with general intelligence rating, with similar scaling on QuALITY and PrOntoQA but mostly flat performance for both Guards and Houdinis on BoolQ, and state that this is consistent with Michael et al. (2023), among prior work finding that judge accuracy may improve with better models. They note prior work tested only a few models.
title: Judge (Guard) performance scaling in LLM debate is consistent with Michael et al.
